messages:
olivia: Heads-up: overnight perf job shows a p99 latency jump ~30% for model-gpt-small when running the fused-attn kernel on A100-p4. CI artifact: link (internal).

infra-bot: nightly-perf/1786123400 completed, tests: text-gen-x1, seq=1024, batch=8.

olivia: Quick paste of the numbers from the run:```baseline(fallback-kernel): p50 48ms p95 82ms p99 120ms throughput 520 req/s
fused-attn: p50 50ms p95 90ms p99 158ms throughput 490 req/s```

kyle: yikes, p99 shape change. p50/p95 fine, so tail problem. Did we change kernel selection policy or seed for batching?

samir: No policy change AFAIK. Last merge that touched kernels was 1785901120 (attn kernel refactor + small memopt). Could be codegen or the new grouping heuristic.

olivia: I re-ran a single-node perf with flags: `--kernel=fused-attn --allow-fallback=false` and saw same tail. With `--kernel=fallback-attn` tails are back to baseline.

bench-runner: I can repro locally. Debug traces show a handful of requests hit an extra memcpy in `kv_cache.cc:insert` on the fused path. Not every request, just those with longer context (>=900).

eva: That matches an observation from the attention RFC: fused path changes KV layout for packing to 128-byte blocks. Could be an alignment-induced extra copy when sequence crosses a block boundary.

kyle: Good clue. Can we add counter metrics around memcpy sizes and count? If it's conditional we can also try a toggle to disable the new packing heuristic.

samir: Suggested fast experiment: 1) bisect commits between 1785800000..1785901120 to find offending change; 2) run microbench that forces seq lengths 880..1024 and log memcpy calls using `env MALLOC_TRACE=1` or `GDB`-backtrace in a perf build.

olivia: I'm on it. Spawning bisect job now (job id bb-1786123). If we find the commit, we should add a correctness check: run `--compare-outputs` between fused and fallback kernels for a small prompt set to ensure no silent divergence.

bench-runner: Also adding a synthetic spike test that runs synthetic-traffic with tail-heavy seq distribution to CI so we catch regressions. Will add to `nightly-perf` as a separate suite.

infra-bot: job bb-1786123 started on a100-p4 pool. ETA ~ 18m.

eva: If it's an alignment/copy problem it's a perf fix but also a correctness risk if truncation/offset math off-by-one. Agree we need deterministic output comparisons.

kyle: For the output comparison, use token-level diff + log-prob A/B for any mismatch. If diff > small epsilon, fail. We'll add that to bench-runner's checklist.

samir: One more thought: the kernel selection layer sometimes re-routes to smaller kernels when queue backlog crosses threshold. Are we sure the fused-attn runs aren't getting starved and then hitting a slow fallback inside the fused code path? Check thread-pool queue times.

bench-runner: Good call — I'm capturing queue latency histograms now. Early look: queue wait distributions unchanged; the extra latency happens after scheduling.

olivia: Update: bisect found candidate commit 1785864005 — a change in `kv_packer.cpp` to improve vectorization. Patch reverts noticeably drop p99 back to baseline in local repro.

kyle: Nice. Next steps: 1) create PR to revert or patch packer logic with perf regression test; 2) land snapshot in canary pool; 3) run compare-output suite and extended nightly.

olivia: I'll open the PR and add the microbench we used as a regression test. Assigning to @samir for kernel review and @eva for correctness guard.

infra-bot: canary deploy queued: canary-1786123456 (3 nodes)

samir: I'll review the packer patch today. If we can keep vectorization but avoid the conditional memcpy on block boundary we should try that first.

eva: I'll draft the compare-output harness and add token-prob thresholds.

olivia: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for status. Will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
